hypothesis: Showing Mexican applicants which documents are accepted, with pictures, before capture raises eventual approval.
population: People starting KYC with a Mexican document. Exclude staff and test accounts, and people already approved.
unit: Person (person_id), assigned at first kyc_started, sticky across attempts.
primary: Eventual approval within 7 days of first start.
window: 7 days per person plus 7 days to mature the last cohort.
sample: Using the recent submission-based Mexican approval rate (78.9%) as a stand-in baseline, about 6,314 people per arm (95% confidence, 80% power). At about 476 Mexican decisions a day that is roughly 27 days at a 50/50 split. Recompute once start-based data exists.
guardrails: Start-to-submit rate, time to decision, fraud-signal rate, support contacts.
rules: Start at 10% for 3 days to check events, then 50/50. Expand if the primary outcome improves by at least the minimum and guardrails hold. Roll back if start-to-submit falls more than 2 pp or fraud signals rise more than 0.5 pp.

hypothesis: Offering one guided retake when liveness returns BAD_QUALITY or FACE_NOT_FULLY_VISIBLE raises eventual approval without raising fraud.
population: People whose first liveness result is BAD_QUALITY or FACE_NOT_FULLY_VISIBLE and who have no fraud signal. Exclude ID_USED_AS_SELFIE and any manipulation label.
unit: Person, assigned at the first eligible liveness failure, sticky.
primary: Eventual approval within 7 days of the failure.
mde: +10 pp on eventual approval in the eligible group.
sample: Assuming about 5% of the eligible group is approved later without a retake (not measurable yet), about 141 people per arm. At about 16 eligible people a day (recent non-incident rate) that is roughly 18 days. Needs the real baseline from instrumentation.
guardrails: Fraud-signal rate and confirmed fraud among retake approvals, liveness spoof labels, vendor cost per approval, time to decision.
rules: Needs Risk sign-off before launch. Start 50/50. Roll back on any confirmed spoof or a fraud-signal rate among retake approvals above control.

kind: Remediation of a confirmed failure (not an A/B test)
hypothesis: Holding and retrying decisions with TECHNICAL_ERROR avoids final rejections caused by execution faults.
population: All decisions with NOT_EXECUTED / TECHNICAL_ERROR in any capability.
unit: Not randomised: withholding a fix for a known failure is not appropriate.
primary: Share of TECHNICAL_ERROR cases resolved after retry, and their eventual approval within 7 days.
sample: Not applicable. Compare with the same incident type before the change.
guardrails: Retry volume and vendor cost, time to decision, approvals among retried cases that later show fraud.
rules: Ship behind a flag. Cap retries at three with backoff, then hold for manual handling. Roll back if retries amplify an outage or cost exceeds the agreed cap.

hypothesis: Reviewing face-match WARNINGs approves a meaningful share of genuine applicants at acceptable quality.
population: Face-match WARNING (NOT_POSSIBLE) cases with no fraud signal; later a sample of NO_MATCH.
primary: Reviewer approval rate and 7-day eventual approval.
mde: Agree with Ops and Risk; for example 30% of reviewed cases approved.
sample: Capacity first: recent volumes are small enough for a pilot (see Plan), but cost per review and service level need Ops input.
guardrails: Second-reviewer agreement on 10% of cases, review turnaround, later fraud among approvals.
rules: Stop if agreement falls below an agreed threshold or turnaround breaches the service level.
